In the [[mathematics|mathematical]] field of [[knot theory]], the '''crosscap number''' of a [[knot (mathematics)|knot]] ''K'' is the minimum of 

:<math>C(K) \equiv 1 - \chi(S), \, </math>

taken over all [[compact space|compact]], [[connected space|connected]], [[orientability|non-orientable]] [[Surface (topology)|surface]]s ''S'' bounding ''K''; here <math>\chi</math> is the [[Euler characteristic]].  The crosscap number of the [[unknot]] is zero, as the Euler characteristic of the disk is one.

==Knot sum==
The crosscap number of a [[knot sum]] is bounded:
:<math>C(k_1) + C(k_2) - 1 \leq C(k_1 \mathbin{\#} k_2) \leq C(k_1) + C(k_2).\,</math>

==Examples==
* The crosscap number of the [[trefoil knot]] is 1, as it bounds a [[Möbius strip]] and is not trivial.
* The crosscap number of a [[torus knot]] was determined by M. Teragaito.

* Teragaito, Masakazu. "Crosscap numbers of torus knots," Topology Appl. 138 (2004), no. 1&ndash;3, 219&ndash;238.
* Teragaito, Masakazu and Hirasawa, Mikami. "Crosscap numbers of 2-bridge knots," Arxiv:math.GT/0504446.
